alignments.note: Noun to noun, split from its article under rule 26.
Verbless clause with a prepositional predicate: rule 53 gives the supplied copula to the preposition, not to the noun-phrase subject; head on the prepositional word.
σου occupies the determiner slot with *thy*, so the article realizes nothing; rule 20.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive.
The ASV writes a bare *Grace* with no determiner; rule 23.
Second verbless clause with a prepositional predicate; the supplied copula rides with the preposition under rule 53, headed on *with*.

review_notes: Both clauses are verbless with prepositional predicates, so rule 53 puts each supplied *be* on μετά rather than on the subject; the ASV's word order *The Lord be* is exactly what rule 53 refuses to read the copula off.
ἡ χάρις has no English determiner, so the article is unrepresented under rule 23 while τοῦ πνεύματός σου is emptied by rule 20 instead.
